name: Höfner
entity_type: Historical German instrument maker / effects brand
dirt_evidence: Fuzz Tone No. 540 / Distortion No. 539 / Guitar Effects Pedal No. 1Z / No. 2Z
notes: Höfner marketed a substantial pedal range from 1967 onward. Its Fuzz Tone No. 540 and later distortion/fuzz combination pedals are documented in period catalog material. Vintage Höfner's archival research says Schaller were heavily involved and that some pedals were also sold with Schaller markings, so Höfner should be preserved as a brand/instrument-maker node with OEM/manufacturing relationships kept separate.

name: Bell Electrolabs
notes: Bell Electrolabs was registered in 1977 by Mike Bell in Stokenchurch, Buckinghamshire. Surviving catalog and company research document a broad module/pedal range including Fuzz and Sustain. Designer Tony Koorlander identified Stan Wilson as the Bell Fuzz designer and described it as an improvement on the Big Muff rather than a simple rebrand.

name: Top Gear
notes: Effects Database documents 18 Top Gear products and identifies Len Hawkes, owner of Hawkes Electronics and a physics lecturer at Brighton Technical College, as designer/manufacturer at Top Gear's Sussex premises. ToneHome documents the rare Fuzz and Fuzz Sustain products and the Series-70 transition in 1975.

name: Lemon StudioSound
notes: Lemon StudioSound was a Karlsruhe manufacturer founded by Gerard Daleiden in the 1970s. ToneHome preserves a 1977 catalog and documents the Zuzz Thainer from 1978, a combined fuzz, sustainer and noise-gate effect. This is a useful German micro-manufacturer node separate from the larger Schaller ecosystem.
